newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas holds on warmer forecast in South.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas holds on warmer forecast in South.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were little changed Friday ahead of a warmer weekend in the South and continued storage buying, industry sources said.

Louisiana Gulf Coast prices at the Henry Hub ranged widely from $2.12 to $2.18 per mmBtu due to a scramble for gas shortly before nomination deadlines, indicating an average gain of one cent from Thursday.

Similarly in south Texas prices held at $2.06-2.08 as a high humidity level in Houston sustained a strong cooling demand, traders said. Temperatures there were expected to stretch to highs around 90 degrees F through midweek.
In the Northeast, New York city gate prices were talked steady to lower in the mid-to-high $2.30s as temperature highs were forecast to reach about 80 degrees F over the weekend.
In the Midwest, prices eased by about one cent to the high-$1.90s, with Chicago city-gate quoted at $2.15-2.18.
Despite the firmness in most markets, west Texas prices were dragged lower today in anticipation of a weaker demand over the weekend and full capacity to southern California, traders said.
Permian prices fell about six cents to about $1.90. Late morning deals were reported done as low as $1.80.
Southern California prices also softened by several cents to about $2.04-2.05.
El Paso Natural Gas Co said its Blanco natural gas plant in the San Juan basin will be shut Monday through Saturday for its annual maintenance outage.

As a result, the pipeline will cut capacity by 240 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) on Monday and by 815 mmcfd on Tuesday and Wednesday. Flows will be cut by 415 mmcfd on Thursday and by 240 mmcfd on Friday and Saturday.
Because of the absent San Juan supply next week, capacity on the North Mainline for deliveries to Topock and South markets will be cut by 195 mmcfd Monday through Thursday for pipeline replacement.
